gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns computability of the L2 projection and unisolvence of the reduced DoF interface: the L2 moments must factor through the preserved DoFs. ISSUE-001 instead diagnoses a regularity mismatch in the node interpolation estimate and its proof. These are different mathematical objects and failed obligations, even though both affect a theorem-level construction.

The gold issue concerns failure to establish serendipity-space membership and differential compatibility by checking reduced DoFs, including the circular use of equality of DoFs. ISSUE-001 concerns only insufficient Sobolev regularity for a node interpolation estimate. It does not recognize the missing reduced-DoF checks, subcomplex inclusion, or circular membership argument.

Both entries identify the same defect in the node interpolation estimate: the stated v in H^s regularity does not provide the H^s regularity of ∇v used on the right-hand side and in the proof, so the bound is not meaningful or valid for the stated class. The prediction also gives the corresponding stronger-regularity or lowered-order repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The node estimate applies an edge/gradient estimate requiring ∇v in H^s while assuming only v in H^s, and it consequently advertises an approximation order one power too high for the stated regularity. The endpoint polynomial counterexample and the corrected regularity/rate alternatives are manifestations of this same missing-regularity and shifted-order obligation.

component_coverage.gold_component: The hypothesis v in H^s does not generally make the displayed H^s seminorm of ∇v available, so the theorem is not meaningful for all stated inputs.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that |∇v|_{s,K} requires ∇v in H^s, equivalently v in H^{s+1}, and that the proof has the same unprovided requirement.

component_coverage.gold_component: The gradient lowers the polynomial degree by one, so the applicable estimate yields h^r, or h^{t-1} for v in H^t, rather than the old h^t estimate.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction identifies that retaining the stated regularity requires lowering the convergence rate by one order, and its repair gives the alternative corrected regularity/rate formulation.

component_coverage.gold_component: The old bound is contradicted at the endpoint because the stated seminorm can vanish for a degree-m gradient while the degree-m node space fails to reproduce the corresponding degree-(m+1) function.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction recognizes the same substantive failure of the advertised estimate for the stated regularity class and supplies the mathematically corresponding stronger-regularity or reduced-rate repair; the omitted explicit polynomial counterexample is only a demonstration detail, not an unrecognized obligation.
